manifest.notes: Onchain guestbook paid in the launch token. LaunchToken (src/LaunchToken.sol) is a fixed-supply ERC-20 with no constructor arguments: name 'Guestbook Token', symbol 'GUEST', 18 decimals, whole supply minted once to its deployer (the factory) in the constructor. It has no owner, mint, pause, blocklist, transfer fee or upgrade path. Its only non-standard surface is burn/burnFrom from OpenZeppelin ERC20Burnable, so supply can only decrease; reviewers should confirm this burn surface is acceptable for the launch token. Guestbook (src/Guestbook.sol) is the single application contract. Its constructor is Guestbook(address token_), nonpayable, and receives $token; it reverts on the zero address or an address without code, so it must deploy after the token. It stores the token as an immutable and grants no role to msg.sender (the factory). sign(string) stores a message of 1 to 280 bytes and burns exactly 10 tokens (10e18 minor units) from the signer through burnFrom, which requires a prior allowance to the guestbook. Entries are append-only. The guestbook has no owner, no privileged role, no pause, no withdraw and no upgrade path, holds no tokens and no ETH, and needs no initialization call; therefore no $owner argument is used. The pool pairs the token with native ETH (zero address). The factory supplies the liquidity position, the MerkleDistributor and the initialization-only pool guard; none of them is a project contract. The manifest fee of 3000 is the admission value; the pool opens at the network trading fee read by the factory. Supply, allocations, owner and policy values come from services, not from this manifest.

LaunchToken has no constructor arguments. Guestbook is configured at deployment with the launch token and has no owner or initialization calls. To sign, callers first approve Guestbook to spend at least 10 GUEST. Each successful sign transfers 10 GUEST (10000000000000000000 base units) to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD; this burn does not reduce ERC-20 totalSupply. Messages are limited to 280 bytes, including empty messages. Entries store the caller, message and block timestamp and are readable by zero-based index through entries(index); entryCount() returns the count. The factory supplies the LP, MerkleDistributor and initialization-only pool guard. Existing tests cover token behavior, deployment, signing, byte limits, payment failures, reentrancy and accounting invariants.

Satoshi Test (SATS) is a plain fixed-supply ERC-20 at src/SatoshiTest.sol (contract SatoshiTest, OpenZeppelin Contracts v5.7.0 ERC20 vendored under lib/, solc 0.8.26, optimizer 200 runs, evm_version paris, bytecode_hash none). The constructor takes no arguments and mints the whole supply of 21,000,000 SATS with 18 decimals, 21000000000000000000000000 minor units, once to msg.sender. In the launch msg.sender is the ProjectFactory, which deploys the token through CREATE2 and holds the entire supply at construction; token.totalSupply above is exactly that amount. There is no owner, minter, pauser, blacklist, fee, burn, hook, receive or fallback: after construction the contract exposes only the ERC-20 interface plus the constant INITIAL_SUPPLY, so the supply can never grow and no privileged call can move or freeze a holder's balance. Every transfer moves exactly the amount asked for, so the factory's transfer of the swarm's share to the MerkleDistributor, the distributor's claim transfers, the single-sided seed through the Uniswap v4 PoolManager and later buys and sells all move whole amounts; the token needs no $factory, $poolManager or $launchNumber exemptions and takes none. No application contracts are deployed and there are no initialization calls. Pool: paired with native ETH (the zero address), fee 3000 (0.30%), tickSpacing 60. initialPrice is provenance only: it is sqrt(21000000e18 / 5e18) * 2^96, the token-per-ETH price implied by economics.initialMarketCapWei (5 ETH) over the full supply with ETH as currency0 and SATS as currency1; the deployer derives the opening price from economics.initialMarketCapWei and token.totalSupply. economics is the requester's and is copied verbatim: 9000 bps of the supply seed the pool at a 5 ETH opening market cap. The swarm's 1000 bps are taken by the factory and are not written here. script/Deploy.s.sol is a standalone operator helper that reads only EXPECTED_CHAIN_ID (31337 or 11155111); it is not used by the factory launch.
